result.title: Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
result.comment: IEEE International Conference on Big Data 2026 (December)
result.summary: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) models are often trained on nominal data using average-risk objectives, which emphasize dominant normal patterns. However, real time series can contain rare but valid nominal regimes that are underrepresented in the training distribution. We show that data-space flow matching can over-penalize such rare-normal windows and assign them anomaly scores comparable to those of true anomalies. To address this, we propose Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching (RT-FM), an unsupervised framework that uses a temporal variational autoencoder to estimate residual latent tailness and converts it into bounded, warmup-annealed weights for training a data-space flow matching model. Experiments on seven TSAD benchmarks show that RT-FM improves rare-normal coverage while preserving strong anomaly discrimination, substantially reducing false alarms on such windows and resulting in improved aggregate detection performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/trustAIoT/RT-FM_time-series-anomaly

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究时间序列异常检测中「稀有但正常的时段」被数据空间 flow matching 过度惩罚、异常分数与真实异常混淆的问题，提出用时序 VAE 估计残差潜变量的尾部程度，并转为有界、warmup 退火的训练权重，在七个基准上降低此类误报。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜空间稀有度估计 + 有界重加权以区分稀有有效模式与真异常」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中如何把罕见但有据的视觉证据/潜在假设与推理失败区分开。
